en: The *Mahāmaṇivipulavimānaviśvasupratiṣṭhitaguhyaparamarahasyakalparājadhāraṇī* (GBM 1724, fol. 53r) states:
"Thirty-two bowls should be filled."
Four [vessels] of oil, four of ghee, four lumps of molasses,
and four filled with sesame seeds.
Four [bowls] should be filled with *aṭhala* fruits;
four should be filled with seven kinds of seeds.
Various offerings (*nānābali*) should be prepared: edible snacks, wrapped sweets, cakes, lentil cakes, and sesame cakes.
Aśokavartika, kālavaṇa, ghṛtagarjaka, and guḍapūpa; all well-prepared offerings should be understood according to what is available.
Having fashioned a well-constructed maṇḍalaka, one should then go to the entrance and place two water-filled jars.

Likewise, having established the offerings and the *bali*, one should perform the ritual of entry accordingly; then, having consecrated [the disciple] with this mantra, one should cause them to enter:
*oṃ maṇi vipula supratiṣṭhita siddha abhiṣiñca māṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaiḥ*.
Bhara bhara saṃbhara hūṃ hūṃ.
As soon as he is consecrated, all hindrances and karmic obstructions accumulated in previous births become completely purified; he becomes embraced by all that is pure,
empowered by all the Tathāgatas, consecrated by all the Tathāgatas, and comforted by all the Tathāgatas.
All accomplishments (*sarvasiddhi*) will become manifest;
whatever one contemplates and whatever one prays for, that very thing he shall accomplish exactly so.

Having entered into the samaya of all Tathāgatas, having followed the true nature (*dharmatā*) of all Tathāgatas, and having attained profound receptivity to the Dharma (*gambhīradharmakṣānti*), he approaches the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*). In this way, he attains such distinguished qualities as these.
Until he becomes irreversible, there is the fulfillment of the path to unsurpassed enlightenment. // § //
5. The third chapter on the ritual procedure for the accomplishment of the maṇḍala. §
GBM 1727 (54v) 1. Now, therefore, I shall explain the characteristics of the mudrās.
Four great heart-mudrās are to be employed by all the Tathāgatas.
2. One should employ the commonality of the family.
The four noble vajra-heart mudrās are to be employed by all maṇḍalas.
Having performed the āśvāsana-mudrā, one should look at another mudrā and begin; this very [mudrā] is to be employed according to the ritual rules within the Tathāgata family.
One should not grasp at external mudrās; rather, other mudrās should be employed everywhere as is convenient, just as they are employed within the Tathāgata family.
Oṃ, heart of all Tathāgatas,
jewel-flame, protect us! Hūṃ.
The Seal of the Heart of the Tathāgata.
Oṃ, of all the Tathāgatas,
the most excellent and supreme jewel, hūṃ!
The Tathāgata Samaya-mudrā.
Oṃ, vajra of the perfect awakening of all Tathāgatas, 3 hūṃ hūṃ.
The Seal of the Tathāgata’s Consolation.
Oṃ, empowerment of all Tathāgatas,
maṇi maṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
The seal of the Tathāgata’s empowerment.
Oṃ, O excellent jewel of all Tathāgatas, beautiful one!
Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
The mudrā of the Tathāgata’s vajra lion throne.
Oṃ, arising from the vastness of all Tathāgatas,
hūṃ hūṃ. This is the Tathāgata-abhiṣeka-mudrā.
Oṃ, the pledge-jewel-vajra of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ hūṃ!
2. Dharmacakra-mudrā: //
Oṃ, O Vajra of all Tathāgatas, victory, unconquered vajra, hūṃ hūṃ!
The Aparājita mudrā.
Oṃ, [to] the great jewel on the peak of the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas, take away, take away, hūṃ hūṃ!
The Tathāgata-Cakravartin Seal.
4 Oṃ, summon all the Tathāgatas with the vajra; hold, hold! Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!
The noble mudrā for grasping the vajra-jewel:
Oṃ dhuru dhuru maṇi mahāvidyuta maṇi svāhā!
The wish-fulfilling jewel mudrā is the mudrā of Noble Vajra.
Oṃ Lokapālite!
Victory, victory! Hūṃ hūṃ!
The mudrās of the four great kings should be taken.
Oṃ, Vipulā, you who are vast,
gather [it] together, hūṃ!
The seal of the Great Goddess Śrī should be taken.
Oṃ, O fanged one, spread forth! Hūṃ!
The tarjanī-mudrā is the third, [belonging to] Śaṅkhinī. Oṃ āgamaya dhīra mucāṭṭa hāsinī hūṃ: the dūtī-mudrā should be bound.
Oṃ samantākāra paripūraṇe dhaka dhaka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mudrā of those who dwell in the maṇḍala.
The āvāhana-mudrā (invocation mudrā) should be assumed.
Oṃ sara sara visara hūṃ hūṃ, [this is] the lotus mudrā.
The fourth detailed chapter on the ritual procedures for mudrās. // § //
Now, therefore, I shall explain the procedure for the cloth painting (*paṭa*), which accomplishes all undertakings;
[it should be made] on a cloth with uncut fringes and free of hair.

On a square surface measuring one or two cubits on each side, a painter observing the *poṣadha* vows should paint the Buddha, the Blessed One, using fresh pigments and not with adhesive ones; he should be depicted seated upon a lion throne,
adorned with all ornaments, surrounded by a gabled pavilion, and preaching the Dharma.
To the right, one should depict Vajrapāṇi with twelve arms, white as an autumn stalk, holding various weapons in his hands, four-faced, and gentle; he should be two digits in width. § //
Now, therefore, I shall explain the procedure for the cloth painting (*paṭalavidhāna*), which accomplishes all undertakings;
[it should be made] on a cloth with uncut fringes.

On a hair-removal ground, one should have the Buddha, the Blessed One, painted by a painter who observes the *poṣadha* vows, using a new vessel and non-adhesive pigments; he should be depicted seated upon a lion throne, surrounded by a gabled pavilion, adorned with all ornaments, and teaching the Dharma, with the area extending one or two cubits on all sides being square.
To the right is Vajrapāṇi;
she should be made with twelve arms, white as an autumn stalk, holding various weapons in her hands, four-faced, and gentle. This is the second [image].
The third face is fierce, and the fourth face is formidable with fangs; it is adorned with a crown of matted hair and a frown, and decorated with all ornaments.
He is seated upon a lotus in the half-lotus posture.
On the left side, the Bodhisattva named Maṇivajra should be depicted, having four faces and sixteen arms.
She offers her right arm, which holds a wish-fulfilling gem, to the Tathāgata.

The two left arms should hold lotuses; two hands should be joined in *añjali*. The remaining five hands should display a trident, a wheel, a sword, a vajra, a flower-vessel, the *kaṇḍula* of Gaṇendra, and a spear.
